a-eb4c9ab7025f04be875e.text: The available records identify 20 Bills and distinguish primary from supporting sponsorship. The lifecycle entries show a mixed picture, with both Current and Lapsed statuses, alongside dated stage activity. These are recorded statuses and events, not a certified account of each Bill’s final fate; treating Current as enactment, or Lapsed as a certified final outcome, would overstate what the records establish.
a-eb4c9ab7025f04be875e.reasoning: The sponsorship search supplies the identified set, while the lifecycle records directly show differing status labels. The distinction between recorded status, dated activity and final outcome follows the limits stated in those records.
limitations: The available records do not certify final outcomes, completeness or freshness.
a-eb4c9ab7025f04be875e.confidenceRationale: The sponsorship count and cited status labels are directly recorded. The summary is limited by unknown freshness and completeness, and status labels do not establish final outcomes.

a-ceb68c89aef87a8c33c0.text: The available sponsorship records identify 20 Bills, but lifecycle evidence has not yet been returned. This draft can therefore set out the recorded sponsorships, but cannot yet report their progress or outcomes.
a-ceb68c89aef87a8c33c0.reasoning: The sponsorship results provide a count of the Bills identified. The lifecycle task remains pending, so there is no accepted status or dated-activity evidence here from which to describe progress or outcomes.
limitations: The sponsorship results are limited to the available records and are not certified as exhaustive.
Lifecycle results, source freshness and final outcomes are not established.
a-ceb68c89aef87a8c33c0.confidenceRationale: The recorded count is directly supported by the sponsorship results. Progress and outcome findings cannot be corroborated because lifecycle evidence is pending.

a-7286e333484c26022a4b.text: The dated entries show substantial recorded stage activity in some cases. Protection of Private Residences (Against Targeted Picketing) Bill 2021 has recorded Committee Stage on 23 May 2024 and Report Stage and Fifth Stage on 4 July 2024. More recently, Artificial Intelligence Companion Services (Protection of Children) Bill 2026 has a recorded Second Stage dated 29 September 2026. The records also contain combinations that should be reported without an inferred procedural explanation: Seanad Electoral (University Members) (Amendment) Bill 2020 is labelled Current while a Bill Lapsed Event and Committee Stage are both recorded on 29 January 2025, followed by another Committee Stage entry on 27 March 2025. Protection of Private Residences (Against Targeted Picketing) Bill 2021 is likewise labelled Current and has a Bill Lapsed Event and Second Stage entry dated 8 November 2024, as well as a further Second Stage entry dated 1 May 2025. These entries establish that the events are recorded, but do not resolve the Bills’ final outcomes.
a-7286e333484c26022a4b.reasoning: This account selects dated stage and lapse entries to illustrate recorded developments and combinations of records that appear inconsistent. It reports each entry separately rather than inferring why the records differ or what ultimately happened to a Bill.
conflicts: For Seanad Electoral (University Members) (Amendment) Bill 2020, the recorded Current status coexists with a Bill Lapsed Event and Committee Stage entries.
For Protection of Private Residences (Against Targeted Picketing) Bill 2021, the recorded Current status coexists with a Bill Lapsed Event and Second Stage entries.
limitations: The lifecycle records do not establish final outcomes or whether these entries are the latest developments.
a-7286e333484c26022a4b.confidenceRationale: The named dates, stages and status labels are directly supported by the lifecycle entries. The records contain material combinations that appear inconsistent, and no evidence supplied explains them or certifies final outcomes.
